##### 7.5.2.3 Manage node labels

You can manage node labels in the Container Service console. You can add a label to multiple nodes at a time, filter nodes by label, and delete labels. You can use labels to schedule nodes. For more information, see Set node schedulability.

**Prerequisites**

##### 7.5.2.4 Set node schedulability

You can mark a node as schedulable or unschedulable in the Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) console. This allows you to optimize the distribution of the loads on each node. This topic describes how to set node schedulability.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the ACK console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**.
3. On the **Clusters** page, find the cluster that you want to manage and click **Details** in the **Actions** column.
4. In the left-side navigation pane of the cluster details page, choose **Nodes > Nodes**.
5. On the Nodes page, select the node that you want to manage and click **Drain/Set to Unschedulable** in
the lower part of the page.

> **Note:** You can also choose **More > Scheduling Settings** in the **Actions** column of the node.

6. In the dialog box that appears, set node schedulability.
If you select **Set to Unschedulable**, pods are not scheduled to this node when you deploy new applications. If you select **Set to Unschedulable and Drain** , pods are not scheduled to this node when you deploy new applications. Pods on this node are evicted, except for the pods that are managed by DaemonSets. In this example, **Set to Unschedulable** is selected.
7. Click **OK**.
The status of the specified node is changed to Unschedulable.

**Results**

Pods are not scheduled to the node when you deploy new applications.

##### 7.5.2.5 Drain nodes

Node draining can safely evict all migratable pods on a node and prevent new pods from being scheduled to the node. This topic describes how to configure node draining. A cluster with only one edge node or worker node does not support the drain operation. Pods that are controlled by DaemonSets are not evicted from the node.

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**.
3. On the **Clusters** page, find the desired cluster and click the name of the cluster in the Cluster Name/ID
column or click **Details** in the **Actions** column.
4. In the left-side navigation pane of the cluster details page, choose **Node > Node**.
5. Drain a single node or multiple nodes.
Drain a single node a. Find the node that you want to drain and choose **More > Drain** in the **Actions** column. Drain multiple nodes a. Select the nodes that you want to drain and click **Drain/Set to Unschedulable** below the node list. b. In the dialog box that appears, select **Set to Unschedulable and Drain** and click **Continue**.
6. In the **Drain** dialog box, set the **Timeout** and read the precautions. Select **I have understood the**
**above instructions and confirmed the execution of the selected operation.** Click **Confirm**
**Eviction**.

> **Note:** **Timeout**: The system automatically fails to run the draining task after the specified timeout period. A value of 0 indicates that no timeout period is specified.

> **Important:** This operation may interrupt your workloads. We recommend that you perform this operation during off-peak hours. If you set the value to Unschedulable, the selected nodes are marked as SchedulingDisabled. Existing pods on the selected nodes can continue to provide services, but newly created pods are no longer scheduled to the nodes.
> After a node is drained, the existing pods on the node will be evicted, except for the pods controlled by DaemonSets, and the node will be marked as SchedulingDisabled. Newly created pods are no longer scheduled to the node.

##### 7.5.2.6 Remove a node

To restart or release an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) node in a cluster, you must first remove the node from the cluster. This topic describes how to remove a node.

**Prerequisites**

A Kubernetes cluster is created. For more information, see Create a Kubernetes cluster. You can connect to the Kubernetes cluster by using kubectl. For more information, see Connect to an ACK cluster by using kubectl.

**Background information**

When you remove a node, pods that run on the node are migrated to other nodes. This may cause service interruption. We recommend that you remove nodes during off-peak hours. Unknown errors may occur when you remove nodes. Before you remove nodes, we recommend that you back up data on these nodes. Nodes remain in the unschedulable state when they are being removed. You can remove only worker nodes. You cannot remove master nodes.

**Procedure**

1. Run the following command to migrate the pods on the node that you want to remove to other nodes.

> **Note:** Make sure that the other nodes have sufficient resources for these pods.

```bash
kubectl drain node-name
```

> **Note:** node-name must be in the format of your-region-name.node-id.
> your-region-name specifies the region where the cluster that you want to manage is deployed.
> node-id specifies the ID of the ECS instance where the node to be removed is deployed. Example: cn-hanghzou.i-xxx.

2. Log on to the ACK console.
3. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**.
4. On the **Clusters** page, find the cluster that you want to manage and click **Details** in the **Actions** column.
5. In the left-side navigation pane of the details page, choose **Nodes > Node**.
6. Find the node that you want to remove and choose **More > Remove** in the **Actions** column.

> **Note:** To remove multiple nodes at a time, select the nodes that you want to remove on the **Nodes** page and click **Batch Remove**.

7. **Optional:**Set parameters in the Remove Node dialog box.
Select **Drain the Node** to migrate the pods on the node to other nodes. If you select this option, make sure that the other nodes have sufficient resources for these pods. Select **Release ECS Instance** to release the ECS instance where the node is deployed.

> **Note:** Select this option to release only pay-as-you-go ECS instances.
> Subscription ECS instances are automatically released after the subscription expires.
> If you do not select **Release ECS Instance**, you are still billed for the ECS instance where the node is deployed.

8. In the **Remove Node** message, click **OK**.

##### 7.5.2.7 View node resource usage

You can view the resource usage of the nodes in a cluster in the Container Service console.

**Prerequisites**

A Kubernetes cluster is created. For more information, see Create a Kubernetes cluster.

**Procedure**

1. Log on to the ACK console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**.
3. On the **Clusters** page, find the cluster that you want to manage and click **Details** in the **Actions** column.
4. In the left-side navigation pane of the details page, choose **Nodes > Nodes**.
5. On the Nodes page, find the node that you want to manage and choose **More > Details** in the **Actions**
column. You can view the request rate and usage rate of CPU and memory resources on each node. CPU request rate = sum (The amount of CPU resources requested by all pods on the node) / Total CPU resources of the node CPU usage rate = sum (The amount of CPU resources used by all pods on the node) / Total CPU resources of the node Memory request rate = (The amount of memory resources requested by all pods on the node) / Total memory resources of the node Memory usage rate = sum (The amount of memory resources used by all pods on the node) / Total memory resources of the node

**Note**

You can adjust the workload of a node based on the resource usage. For more information, see Set node schedulability.

> When the request or usage rate of a node reaches 100%, pods are not scheduled to the node.

#### 7.5.3 Hybrid cloud node pools

##### 7.5.3.1 Create and manage hybrid node pools

This approach allows you to unify management of your cloud and on-premises resources, enabling elastic scheduling and cost optimization while leveraging your existing IT assets.

**Prerequisites**

Before you create a hybrid node pool, ensure you meet the following requirements: You have a Kubernetes cluster of version 1.32 or later. You have at least three ECS nodes in your cluster to run ACK control plane components and ensure high availability. You have installed the Terway-Hybrid and terway-hybrid-controlplane components. The following components must meet these minimum version requirements: ube-flannel-ds: >= v0.15.1.23-33d25c1-aliyun csi-plugin and csi-provisioner: >= v1.34.1 terway-eniip: >= v1.13.9.1 flannel (vxlan): >= v0.15.1.23-20a397e6-aliyun

**Impact assessment**

To prevent disruptions to existing workloads in your ACK cluster, nodes in a hybrid node pool are automatically configured with the following label and taint:

```
apiVersion: v1 kind: Node metadata:
  labels:
    alibabacloud.com/nodepool-type: hybridcloud
... spec:
  taints:
  - effect: NoSchedule
    key: nodepool-type
    value: "hybridcloud"
...
```

To schedule Pods on these hybrid nodes, you must add a matching toleration to your Pods. If your applications do not need to differentiate between cloud and on-premises nodes, you can also remove the taint. However, do not remove the default label `alibabacloud.com/nodepool-type: hybridcloud` , as removing it may affect product functionality.

**Create a hybrid node pool**

You can configure the node pool, including its basic and network settings, in the console. Some settings, particularly those related to availability and networking, cannot be modified after creation. Creating a new node pool does not affect the nodes or workloads in any existing node pools.
1. Log on to the Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) console. In the left-side navigation pane, click
**Clusters**.
2. On the **Clusters** page, click the name of your target dedicated cluster. In the left-side navigation pane,
choose **Node Management > Node Pools**.
3. On the **Node Pools** page, click **Create Hybrid Cloud Node Pool**.
4. On the **Create Hybrid Cloud Node Pool** page, configure the required parameters and click **Submit**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Node pool name | Enter a name for the node pool. |
| Region | Select the region where you want to deploy the node pool. |
| Zone | You can select an existing zone or specify a custom one. Manual Input: Specify a logical zone name, such as idc-zone-1 , that is unique within the cluster. |

| Container runtime | Only containerd is supported. The available runtime version depends on the cluster version. |
|---|---|
| Network plugin | Currently, only Terway-Hybrid is supported. This network plugin provides network connectivity for Pods between your data center and the cloud. |
| Network type | Currently, only overlay is supported. The overlay network is easy to configure, independent of the underlying network, and flexible to deploy. |
| Node labels | Add labels to the nodes in this node pool. |
| Taints | Add taints to the worker nodes in this node pool. |

> **Note:** After the node pool is created, you can perform the following actions:
> To modify the node pool, click **Edit** in the **Actions** column.
> To view node pool details, click **Details** in the **Actions** column.
> To delete the node pool, click **Delete** in the **Actions** column.

**Add hybrid nodes**

You can add your own hybrid nodes to an ACK cluster as worker nodes and manage them centrally in the ACK console.

**Standard hybrid nodes**

i. On the **Node Pools** page, in the **Actions** column of the target node pool, click **Add Existing Node**. ii. Click **Copy** in the upper-right corner of the script box, and run the script on the target node to add it to the cluster.

**BMS instances as worker nodes**

i. On the **Node Pools** page, in the **Actions** column of the target node pool, click **Add Existing Node**. ii. Click **Copy** in the upper-right corner of the script box. Append your BMS instance ID to the end of the script, replacing the `i-xxxxx` placeholder.

```
...... --instance-id i-xxxxx
```

iii. Log on to the BMS instance and run the script on the node to add it to the cluster.

**Remove hybrid nodes**

1. On the **Node Pools** page, in the **Actions** column of the target node pool, click **Remove Node**.
2. In the dialog box, review the information, optionally select the **Drain Node** checkbox, and click **OK**.

##### 7.5.3.2 Work with Terway Hybrid

When hybrid cloud node pools are connected to on-premises data centers, the complex network topology and cross-domain routing requirements exceed the capabilities of conventional container network plug-ins. Terway Hybrid, a network plug-in specifically designed for hybrid cloud node pools, ensures seamless network connectivity between pods (on-premises or in the cloud) within the cluster.

**How Terway Hybrid works**

The following figure shows the overall network architecture of hybrid cloud node pools for Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK). The architecture is divided into two network domains: Apsara Stack central VPC and data center. (If multiple data centers or third-party clouds are interconnected with the central VPC, additional network domains exist.) Layer 3 intranet connectivity is established between these two network domains through Express Connect circuits. Within this architecture, the ACK cluster in the central VPC can use either the Flannel or Terway network plug-in, while the data center uses the Terway Hybrid network plug-in.

**Terway Hybrid mode**

Terway Hybrid provides the Overlay mode at the node pool level. You can configure the Overlay mode when you create and manage hybrid cloud node pools.

**Overlay mode**

**Benefits**: It features simple configuration, has no special requirements on the underlying network, and
offers flexible deployment.
**Network requirements**: Only Layer 3 intranet connectivity is required between nodes.
**Container network path**: Container network packets are VXLAN-encapsulated through virtual network
interfaces and transmitted over UDP using host port 8472.

**Prerequisites**

An ACK cluster is created, and its Kubernetes version is 1.32 or later. When you use a hybrid cloud node pool, you should also retain Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instances to deploy certain ACK control plane components. We recommend that at least three ECS instances be used to ensure high availability. The terway-hybrid and terway-hybrid-controlplane components are installed. Components are updated to meet the following version requirements: ube-flannel-ds: v0.15.1.23-33d25c1-aliyun or later csi-plugin and csi-provisioner: v1.34.1 or later terway-eniip: v1.13.9.1 or later flannel (vxlan): v0.15.1.23-20a397e6-aliyun or later

**Procedure**

1. Log in to the Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) console.
2. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**.
3. On the **Clusters** page, click the name of the cluster that you want to manage. In the left-side navigation
pane, click **Add-ons**.
4. On the **Add-ons** page, find the **terway-hybrid-controlplane** component card and click **Install**.
5. Configure the following parameters and click **OK**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| RemoteContainerCIDR | The IPv4 CIDR block for pods in this hybrid cloud node pool. A subnet will be allocated from this CIDR block to each node. The CIDR block for pods cannot overlap with the CIDR blocks of an existing Service, pod, or VPC. Sample CIDR block format: 192.168.0.1/16 . Important Configure this parameter based on your business requirements. After you configure this parameter, it cannot be modified. |
| RemoteContainerCIDRM askSize | The size of the IPv4 subnet mask assigned to each hybrid cloud node. Valid values: 24 to 28. Important Configure this parameter based on your business requirements. After you configure this parameter, it cannot be modified. |
| Enable SNAT | Specifies whether to convert the source IP address to the IP address of the hybrid cloud node when the pod of the node accesses the external endpoint of the cluster. |

6. On the **Add-ons** page, find the **terway-hybrid** component and click **Install**.
When you install the **terway-hybrid** data plane component, you do not need to configure parameters. Subsequently added hybrid cloud nodes will automatically have the Terway Hybrid plug-in installed.

### 7.6 Storage

#### 7.6.1 Overview

You can create disk volumes and Object Storage Service (OSS) volumes in the Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) console to enable data persistence for stateful applications. Both statically provisioned volumes and dynamically provisioned volumes are supported. The following table describes the types of volumes that are supported by different storage services of Apsara Stack.

| Apsara Stack storage service | Statically provisioned volume | Dynamically provisioned volume |
|---|---|---|
| Alibaba Cloud disks | You can mount a statically provisioned disk volume by using a persistent volume (PV) and a persistent volume claim (PVC). | Supported |
| File Storage NAS (NAS) | You can mount a statically provisioned NAS volume by using a PV and a PVC. | Supported |
| OSS | You can mount a statically provisioned OSS volume by using a PV and a PVC | Supported |

#### 7.6.2 Mount disk volumes

You can mount disks as volumes. Container Service allows you to mount disks as persistent volumes (PVs) in Kubernetes clusters. Disks can be mounted to Kubernetes clusters as the following volume types: Statically provisioned disk volumes You can use statically provisioned disk volumes in the following ways: Mount disks as volumes Mount disk volumes by creating a PV and a persistent volume claim (PVC) Dynamically provisioned disk volumes

**Usage notes**

You can mount a disk only to one pod. Before you mount a disk to a pod, you must create the disk and obtain its disk ID. The disk must meet the following capacity requirements: If the disk is a basic disk, it must be at least 5 GiB in size. If the disk is an ultra disk, it must be at least 20 GiB in size. If the disk is a standard SSD, it must be at least 20 GiB in size. volumeId: the ID of the disk that you want to mount. The value must be the same as those of volumeName and PV Name. A disk can be mounted only to a node that is deployed in the same zone as the disk. Only pay-as-you-go disks can be mounted. If you change the billing method of an Elastic Compute Service (ECS) instance in the cluster from pay-as-you-go to subscription, you cannot change the billing method of its disks to subscription. Otherwise, the disks cannot be mounted to the cluster.

**Statically provisioned disk volumes**

You can mount disks as volumes or by creating PVs and PVCs.

**Prerequisites**

A disk is created in the ECS console.

**Mount a disk as a volume**

Use the following disk-deploy.yaml file to create a pod:

```
apiVersion: extensions/v1beta1 kind: Deployment metadata:
  name: nginx-disk-deploy
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx-flexvolume-disk
        image: nginx
        volumeMounts:
          - name: "d-bp1j17ifxfasvts3tf40"
            mountPath: "/data"
      volumes:
        - name: "d-bp1j17ifxfasvts3tf40"
          flexVolume:
            driver: "alicloud/disk"
            fsType: "ext4"
            options:
              volumeId: "d-bp1j17ifxfasvts3tf40"
```

**Mount disk volumes by creating a PV and a PVC**

i. **Create a PV of the disk type** You can create a PV of the disk type in the Container Service console or by using a YAML file.

**Create a PV by using a YAML file**

Use the following `disk-pv.yaml` file to create a PV:

> **Note:** The PV name must be the same as the disk ID.

```
apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolume metadata:
  name: d-bp1j17ifxfasvts3tf40
  labels:
    failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/zone: cn-hangzhou-b
    failure-domain.beta.kubernetes.io/region: cn-hangzhou
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 20Gi
  storageClassName: disk
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  flexVolume:
    driver: "alicloud/disk"
    fsType: "ext4"
    options:
      volumeId: "d-bp1j17ifxfasvts3tf40"
```

**Create a PV in the console**

a. Log on to the Container Service console. b. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**. c. On the **Clusters** page, find the cluster that you want to manage and click **Details** in the **Actions** column. d. In the left-side navigation pane of the details page, choose **Volumes > Persistent Volumes**. e. On the **Persistent Volumes** page, click **Create** in the upper-right corner. f. In the Create PV dialog box, set the parameters. Table 1. PV parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PV Type | In this example, Cloud Disk is selected. |
| Volume Plug-in | Displays the supported storage drivers. |
| Access Mode | By default, ReadWriteOnce is selected. |
| Disk ID | Select a disk that is in the same region and zone as your cluster. |
| File System Type | Select the file system of the disk. Supported file systems are ext4, ext3, xfs, and vfat. Default value: ext4. |
| Label | Add labels to the PV. |

g. Click **Create**. ii. **Create a PVC** Use the following `disk-pvc.yaml` file to create a PVC:

```
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim apiVersion: v1 metadata:
  name: pvc-disk
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: disk
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 20Gi
```

iii. **Create a pod** Use the following disk-pod.yaml file to create a pod:

```
apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata:
  name: "flexvolume-alicloud-example"
spec:
  containers:
    - name: "nginx"
      image: "nginx"
      volumeMounts:
        - name: pvc-disk
          mountPath: "/data"
  volumes:
  - name: pvc-disk
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: pvc-disk
```

**Dynamically provisioned disk volumes**

To mount a disk as a dynamically provisioned volume, you must create a StorageClass of the disk type and specify the StorageClass in the storageClassName field of the PVC.
1. **Create a StorageClass**

```
kind: StorageClass apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1beta1 metadata:
  name: alicloud-disk-common-hangzhou-b
provisioner: alicloud/disk parameters:
  type: cloud_ssd
  regionid: cn-hangzhou
  zoneid: cn-hangzhou-b
```

Required parameters: provisioner: Set this parameter to alicloud/disk. This indicates that the Provisioner plug-in is used to create the StorageClass. type: Specify the disk type. Valid values: cloud, cloud_efficiency, cloud_ssd, and available. If you set this parameter to available, the system attempts to create a disk in the following order: ultra disk, standard SSD, and basic disk. The system stops trying until a disk is created. regionid: Specify the region of the disk. zoneid: Specify the zone of the disk.

```
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim apiVersion: v1 metadata:
  name: disk-common
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: alicloud-disk-common-hangzhou-b
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 20Gi
--kind: Pod apiVersion: v1 metadata:
  name: disk-pod-common
spec:
  containers:
  - name: disk-pod
    image: nginx
    volumeMounts:
      - name: disk-pvc
        mountPath: "/mnt"
  restartPolicy: "Never"
  volumes:
    - name: disk-pvc
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: disk-common
```

**Default options**

By default, Kubernetes clusters support the following types of StorageClass: alicloud-disk-common: basic disk. alicloud-disk-efficiency: ultra disk. alicloud-disk-ssd: standard SSD. alicloud-disk-available: This option ensures high availability. The system attempts to create an ultra disk first. If no ultra disk is available in the specified zone, the system attempts to create a standard SSD. If no standard SSD is available, the system attempts to create a basic disk.
3. **Create a multi-instance StatefulSet by using a disk**
We recommend that you use the volumeClaimTemplates parameter. This parameter allows the system to dynamically create PVCs and PVs. PVCs are associated with corresponding PVs.

```
apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata:
  name: nginx
  labels:
    app: nginx
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 80
    name: web
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: nginx
--apiVersion: apps/v1beta2 kind: StatefulSet metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  serviceName: "nginx"
  replicas: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          name: web
        volumeMounts:
        - name: disk-common
          mountPath: /data
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: disk-common
    spec:
      accessModes: [ "ReadWriteOnce" ]
      storageClassName: "alicloud-disk-common"
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 10Gi
```

#### 7.6.3 Mount a statically provisioned NAS volume

File Storage NAS (NAS) is a distributed file system that supports shared access, elastic scaling, high reliability, and high performance. This topic describes how to mount a statically provisioned NAS volume. This topic also describes how to enable persistent storage and shared storage by using a statically provisioned NAS volume.

**Prerequisites**

A NAS file system is created in the NAS console and a mount target is created for the NAS file system. You can use the mount target to mount the NAS file system to your cluster. The NAS file system and your cluster belong to the same virtual private cloud (VPC). For more information, see **File Storage NAS User Guide**.

**Scenarios**

Your application requires high disk I/O. You need a storage service that offers higher read and write throughput than Object Storage Service (OSS). You want to share files across hosts. For example, you want to use a NAS file system as a file server.

**Usage notes**

If a NAS file system is mounted to multiple pods, the data in the file system is shared by the pods. In this case, the application must be able to synchronize data across the pods if the data in the NAS file system is modified by multiple pods.

> **Note:** You cannot grant permissions to access the / directory (root directory) of the NAS file system. The user account and user group to which the directory belongs cannot be modified.

Statically provisioned NAS volumes cannot be expanded. If the **securityContext.fsgroup** parameter is specified in the application template, kubelet performs the `chmod` or `chown` operation after the volume is mounted, which increases the time consumption. You can delete this parameter to reduce the time consumption of volume mounting.

**Mount a statically provisioned NAS volume in the console**

1. Create a persistent volume (PV).
i. Log on to the ACK console. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**. ii. On the **Clusters** page, find the cluster that you want to manage and click its name. You can also click
**Details** in the **Actions** column to go to the cluster details page.
iii. In the left-side navigation pane, choose **Volumes > Persistent Volumes**. iv. In the upper-right corner of the **Persistent Volumes** page, click **Create**. v. In the **Create PV** dialog box, configure the parameters described in the following table and click
**Create**.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PV Type | The type of the PV. Valid values: Cloud Disk, NAS, and OSS. In this example,N AS is selected. |
| Volume Name | The name of the PV. The name must be unique within the cluster. In this example, pv-nas is used. |
| Volume Plug-in | The type of the storage driver that is used to provision the volume. You can select only CSI. |
| Capacity | The capacity claimed by the PV. Note A NAS file system provides unlimited capacity. This parameter does not limit the storage usage of the NAS file system but defines the capacity of the PV. |
| Access Mode | The access mode of the PV. Valid values: ReadWriteMany or ReadWriteOnce. Default value: ReadWriteMany. |
| Mount Target Domain Name | The mount target of the NAS file system. You can select a mount target or specify a custom mount target. |
| Show Advanced Options | Subdirectory: the subdirectory of the NAS file system that you want to mount. The subdirectory must start with a forward slash (/). After you configure this parameter, the PV is mounted to the subdirectory. If the specified subdirectory does not exist, the system automatically creates the subdirectory in the NAS file system and mounts the subdirectory to the cluster. If you leave this parameter empty, the root directory of the NAS file system is mounted. If you want to mount an Extreme NAS file system, the subdirectory must be under the /share directory. Version: the version of the PV. |
| Labels | The labels that you want to add to the PV. |

2. Create a persistent volume claim (PVC).
i. In the left-side navigation pane of the cluster details page, choose **Volumes > Persistent Volume**
**Claims**.
ii. In the upper-right corner of the **Persistent Volume Claims** page, click **Create**. iii. In the **Create PVC** dialog box, configure the parameters described in the following table.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| PVC Type | The type of the PVC. Valid values: Cloud Disk, NAS, and OSS. In this example,N AS is selected. |
| Volume Name | The name of the PVC. The name must be unique within the cluster. |
| Allocation Mode | Specifies how the PVC is bound to a PV. In this example, Existing Volume is selected. Note If no PV is created, you can set theA llocation Mode parameter to Create Volume and configure the required parameters to create a PV. For more information, see the Create a PV section of this topic. |
| Existing Volume | Click Select PV. In the dialog box that appears, find the PV that you want to use and click Select in the Actions column. |
| Capacity | The capacity claimed by the PVC. Note The capacity claimed by the PVC cannot exceed the capacity of the PV that is bound to the PVC. |

iv. After you complete the configuration, click **Create**. After the PVC is created, you can view the PVC in the PVC list. The PVC is bound to the corresponding PV.
3. Create an application. For more information, see Create a stateless workload (Deployment).
In the **Container** step, configure the parameters described in the following table in the Volume section. In this example, a cloud volume is used. Set the **PV Type** parameter to **Cloud Storage**, the **Mount Source** `/tmp`. parameter to **csi-nas-pvc**, and the **Container Path** parameter to

| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| Local storage | Click Add Local Storage and configure the PV Type, Mount Source, and Container Path parameters to mount the volume to a container path. TheS ubpath parameter is optional. By default, this parameter is left empty. You can select HostPath, ConfigMap, Secret, or EmptyDir from the PV Type drop-down list. For more information, see Volumes. |
| Cloud storage | Click Add PVC and configure the PV Type, Mount Source, and Container Path parameters to mount the volume to a container path. The Subpath parameter is optional. By default, this parameter is left empty. You can select only Cloud Storage from the PV Type drop-down list. |

**Mount a statically provisioned NAS volume by using kubectl**

1. Create a statically provisioned PV.
i. Create a file named pv-nas.yaml and copy the following content to the file:

```
apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolume metadata:
  name: pv-nas
  labels:
    alicloud-pvname: pv-nas
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 5Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  csi:
    driver: nasplugin.csi.alibabacloud.com
    volumeHandle: pv-nas
    volumeAttributes:
      server: "2564f4****-ysu87.cn-shenzhen.nas.aliyuncs.com"
      path: "/csi"
  mountOptions:
  - nolock,tcp,noresvport
  - vers=3
```

The following table describes the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| name | The name of the PV. |
| labels | The labels that you want to add to the PV. |
| storage | The capacity of the NAS volume. |
| accessModes | The access mode of the PV. |
| driver | The type of the storage driver that is used to provision the volume. In this example, the parameter is set to nasplugin.csi.alibabacloud.com . This indicates that the NAS Container Storage Interface (CSI) plug-in provided by Apsara Stack is used. |
| volumeHandle | The unique identifier of the PV. If multiple PVs are used, the identifier of each PV must be unique. |
| server | The mount target of the NAS file system. |
| path | The subdirectory of the NAS file system that you want to mount. If you want to mount an Extreme NAS file system, the subdirectory must be under the /share directory. |
| vers | The version of the Network File System (NFS) protocol. We recommend that you use NFSv3. Extreme NAS file systems support only NFSv3. |

ii. Run the following command to create a statically provisioned PV:

```bash
kubectl create -f pv-nas.yaml
```

2. Create a static PVC.
i. Create a file named pvc-nas.yaml and copy the following content to the file: When you create a PVC of the NAS type, specify the `selector` parameter to configure how a PV is bound to the PVC.

```
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim apiVersion: v1 metadata:
  name: pvc-nas
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      alicloud-pvname: pv-nas
```

The following table describes some parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| name | The name of the PVC. |
| accessModes | The access mode of the PVC. |
| storage | The capacity claimed by the PVC. The claimed capacity cannot exceed the capacity of the PV that is bound to the PVC. |
| matchLabels | The labels that are used to select a PV and bind it to the PVC. |

ii. Run the following command to create a PVC used for static provisioning:

```bash
kubectl create -f pvc-nas.yaml
```

3. Create an application that has the PVC mounted.
i. Create a file named nas.yaml and copy the following content to the file. You can use the file to create an application named nas-static.

```
apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata:
  name: nas-static
  labels:
    app: nginx
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        volumeMounts:
          - name: pvc-nas
            mountPath: "/data"
      volumes:
        - name: pvc-nas
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: pvc-nas
```

The following table describes some parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| image | The image address of the application. Replace it with the actual image address that you want to use. |
| mountPath | The path of the container to which the NAS volume is mounted. |
| claimName | The name of the PVC mounted to the application. |

ii. Run the following command to create an application named nas-static and mount the created PVC to the application:

```bash
kubectl create -f nas.yaml
```

4. Run the following command to query the pods that run the application:

```bash
kubectl get pod
```

Expected output:


#### 7.6.4 Use dynamic NAS volumes

NAS volumes are ideal for scenarios such as big data analytics, data sharing, web applications, and log persistence. Instead of using static volumes, you can dynamically provision storage by creating a persistent volume claim (PVC) and configuring a StorageClass. The system then automatically provisions a persistent volume for you, eliminating the need to manually create and configure storage resources. You can mount dynamic NAS volumes using either the subpath or filesystem method.

**Prerequisites**

You have created a Container Service for Kubernetes (ACK) cluster. You have created a NAS file system. For more information, see the **"Create a file system"** section of the
**Quick Start** chapter in the **File System NAS User Guide**.
If you need to encrypt data on the NAS volume, specify an encryption type when you create the NAS file system. You have created a NAS mount target. For more information, see the **"Add a mount target"** section of the **Quick Start** chapter in the **File System NAS User Guide**. The NAS mount target must be in the same VPC as your cluster nodes.

**Use cases**

Applications that have high disk I/O requirements. Scenarios that require higher read and write performance than Object Storage Service (OSS). File sharing across hosts, such as for a file server.

**Considerations**

When you use an Extreme Speed NAS file system, the `path` that you configure in the StorageClass for a dynamic volume must use /share as the parent directory. For example, `0cd8b4a576-g****.cn-` `hangzhou.nas.aliyuncs.com:/share/subpath` indicates that the subdirectory of the NAS file system mounted

| /share/subpath | . |
|---|---|

A NAS file system can be mounted by multiple pods simultaneously. In this case, your application is responsible for implementing data synchronization to prevent conflicts from concurrent modifications.

> **Note:** You cannot change the permissions, owner, or group of the root directory ( `/` ) of a NAS volume.

If you configure the **securityContext.fsgroup** parameter in your application template, kubelet runs the `chmod` or `chown` command after the storage volume is mounted, prolonging the mount time.

**Use dynamic NAS volumes in the console**

From the console, you can create only subpath-type dynamic NAS volumes. To use a filesystem-type dynamic NAS volume, you must use kubectl.

**Step 1: Create a StorageClass**

1. Log on to the ACK console. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**.
2. On the **Clusters** page, click the name of the target dedicated cluster. In the left-side navigation pane,
choose **Storage > StorageClasses**.
3. On the **StorageClasses** page, click **Create** in the upper-right corner.
4. In the **Create** dialog box, configure the parameters for the StorageClass.
The following table describes some of the key parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Name | The name of the StorageClass. The name must start with a lowercase letter and can contain only lowercase letters, digits, periods (.), and hyphens (-). |
| Volume type | You can select Cloud Disk, NAS, or OSS. In this example, select NAS. |
| Provisioner | Select CSI. |
| Reclaim policy | The reclaim policy. The default value is Delete , but Retain is also supported. Delete mode: Must be used with the archiveOnDelete parameter. If archiveOnDelete is set to true , when the PVC is deleted, the persistent volume (PV) and its corresponding NAS file are renamed instead of deleted. If archiveOnDelete is set to false , when the PVC is deleted, the PV and the NAS file are permanently deleted. Retain mode: When the PVC is deleted, the PV and the NAS file system are not deleted. You must delete them manually. If data security is a high priority, we recommend using the Retain policy to prevent accidental data loss. |
| Mount target | The mount target address of the NAS file system. If no mount target addresses are available, create a NAS file system first. |
| Path | The mount path in the NAS file system. |

| Mount options | Optional parameters for mounting the NAS file system, such as the NFS protocol version. |
|---|---|

5. After you configure the parameters, click **Create**.
After the StorageClass is created, it appears in the **StorageClasses** list.

**Step 2: Create a PVC**

1. In the left-side navigation pane of the cluster management page, choose **Storage > Persistent Volume**
**Claims**.
2. On the **Persistent Volume Claims** page, click **Create** in the upper-right corner.
3. In the **Create Persistent Volume Claim** dialog box, configure the parameters.

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| Persistent volume claim type | The supported storage types are Cloud Disk, NAS, and OSS. For this example, select NAS. |
| Name | The name of the PVC. The name must be unique within the cluster. |
| Provisioning mode | For this example, select Dynamic Provisioning Using StorageClass. |
| Existing StorageClass | Click Select StorageClass. In the Select StorageClass dialog box, find the target StorageClass and click Select in the Actions column. |
| Total capacity | The capacity of the volume to be created. |
| Access mode | The default value is ReadWriteMany . You can also select ReadWriteOnce . |

|   | ReadWriteMany |
|---|---|
| ReadWriteOnce |   |

4. Click **Create**.
After the PVC is created, it appears in the list and is bound to a corresponding volume.

**Step 3: Create an application**

1. In the left-side navigation pane of the cluster management page, choose **Workloads > Deployments**.
2. On the **Deployments** page, click **Create from Image**.
3. Configure the parameters to create the application, and then click **Create**.
The following table describes the key parameters. You can keep the default values for the other parameters. For more information, see Create a stateless application by using a Deployment.

| Section | Parameter | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basic informati on | Applicatio n name | The name of the Deployment. Follow the format requirements shown in the UI. | nas-test |
|   | Replicas | The number of replicas for the Deployment. | 2 |
|   | Image name | The address of the image used to deploy the application. | anolis-registry.cn- zhangjiakou.cr.aliyuncs.com/ope nanolis/nginx:1.14.1-8.6 |

| ntainer Serv | ice for Kubernetes User Guide·Kubernetes clusters |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|
| Container configura tion |   |   |   |
|   | Required resources | The required vCPU and memory resources. | 0.25 Core, 512 MiB |
|   | Volume | Click Add Existing PersistentVolumeClaim and configure the parameters. Volume: Select the PVC you created earlier. Mount Path: Enter the path in the container where the NAS file system will be mounted. | Mount Source: pvc-nas Mount Path: /data |

4. Check the deployment status of the application.
i. On the **Deployments** page, click the name of the application. ii. Click the **Pods** tab and confirm that the pod status is **Running**.

**Use dynamic NAS volumes with kubectl**

**Use a subpath dynamic NAS volume**

Use a subpath-type dynamic NAS volume when multiple Kubernetes applications or pods need to share data by mounting the same NAS volume, or when different pods need to mount different subdirectories of the same NAS file system. When you use the subpath method to mount a dynamic NAS volume, you must manually create the NAS file system and mount target.
1. Create a NAS file system and a mount target. For more information, see the **"Create a file system"** and
**"Add a mount target"** sections in the **Quick Start** chapter of the **File System NAS User Guide**.
2. Create a StorageClass.
i. Create a file named alicloud-nas-subpath.yaml and copy the following content into it.

```
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1 kind: StorageClass metadata:
  name: alicloud-nas-subpath
mountOptions:
- nolock,tcp,noresvport
- vers=3
parameters:
  volumeAs: subpath
  server: "0cd8b4a576-g****.cn-hangzhou.nas.aliyuncs.com:/k8s/"
provisioner: nasplugin.csi.alibabacloud.com reclaimPolicy: Retain
```

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| mountOptions | The options parameter for mounting a NAS is configured in mountOptions, including the NFS protocol version. |
| volumeAs | Valid values are subpath and filesystem . These values specify whether to create a PV for a subdirectory or an entire file system, respectively. |
| server | The mount target address of the NAS file system when creating a subpath-type PV. |
| provisioner | Driver type. In this example, the value is nasplugin.csi.alibabacloud.com , which indicates that the Alibaba Cloud NAS CSI plugin is used. |
| reclaimPolicy | The reclaim policy for the PV. The default value is Delete , but Retain is also supported. Delete mode: Must be used with the archiveOnDelete parameter. If archiveOnDelete is set to true , when the PVC is deleted, the PV and its corresponding NAS file are renamed instead of deleted. If archiveOnDelete is set to false , when the PVC is deleted, the PV and NAS file are permanently deleted. Retain mode: When the PVC is deleted, the PV and the NAS file system are not deleted. You must delete them manually. If data security is a high priority, we recommend using the Retain policy to prevent accidental data loss. |
| archiveOnDelete | Specifies whether to delete the backend storage when reclaimPolicy is set to Delete. This option, configured in the parameters section, acts as a safeguard for shared storage systems such as NAS. By default, the value is true, which renames the directory or file to archived-{pvName}.{timestamp} instead of deleting it. If you set the value to false, the backend storage resource is permanently deleted. |

ii. Run the following command to create the StorageClass:

```bash
kubectl create -f alicloud-nas-subpath.yaml
```

3. Create a PVC.
i. Create a file named pvc.yaml and copy the following content into it.

```
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim apiVersion: v1 metadata:
  name: nas-csi-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteMany
  storageClassName: alicloud-nas-subpath
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 20Gi
```

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| name | The name of the PVC. |
| accessModes | The access mode. |
| storageClassName | The name of the StorageClass to bind. |
| storage | The storage capacity requested by the application. Note The capacity specified here does not limit the actual capacity that the application can use and does not trigger automatic expansion. A quota is set for the NAS directory only when you use a General-purpose NAS file system and the allowVolumeExpansion parameter in the StorageClass is set to true. |

ii. Run the following command to create the PVC:

```bash
kubectl create -f pvc.yaml
```

4. Create an application.
Create two applications, **nginx-1** and **nginx-2**, that share the same subdirectory of the NAS volume. i. Create a file named nginx-1.yaml and copy the following content into it.

```
apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata:
  name: deployment-nas-1
  labels:
    app: nginx-1
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx-1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx-1
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: anolis-registry.cn-zhangjiakou.cr.aliyuncs.com/openanolis/nginx:1.14.1-8.6
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        volumeMounts:
          - name: nas-pvc
            mountPath: "/data"
      volumes:
        - name: nas-pvc
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: nas-csi-pvc
```

`mountPath` : The path in the container where the NAS file system is mounted. `claimName` : The name of the PVC to bind. In this example, the value is **nas-csi-pvc**. ii. Create a file named nginx-2.yaml and copy the following content into it.

```
apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata:
  name: deployment-nas-2
  labels:
    app: nginx-2
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx-2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx-2
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: anolis-registry.cn-zhangjiakou.cr.aliyuncs.com/openanolis/nginx:1.14.1-8.6
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        volumeMounts:
          - name: nas-pvc
            mountPath: "/data"
      volumes:
        - name: nas-pvc
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: nas-csi-pvc
```

`mountPath` : The path in the container where the NAS volume is mounted. For example, /data. `claimName` : Enter the same PVC name as the **nginx-1** application. In this example, the name is **nas-**
**csi-pvc**.
iii. Run the following command to create the **nginx-1** and **nginx-2** applications:

```bash
kubectl create -f nginx-1.yaml -f nginx-2.yaml
```

5. Run the following command to view pod information:

```bash
kubectl get pod
```

Expected output:

```
NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE deployment-nas-1-5b5cdb85f6-n**** 1/1 Running 0 32s deployment-nas-2-c5bb4746c-4**** 1/1 Running 0 32s
```

> **Note:** Mounting the same subdirectory `/data` of a NAS file system to different Pods means that the NAS volume with the mount target `0cd8b4a576-g****.cn-hangzhou.nas.aliyuncs.com:/k8s/nas-79438493-`

|   | f3e0-11e9-bbe5-00163e09**** |   |
|---|---|---|
|   | nas-1-5b5cdb85f6-a**** | deployment-nas-2-c5bb4746c-b**** |

> `/k8s` is the subpath specified in the StorageClass.
> `nas-79438493-f3e0-11e9-bbe5-00163e09****` is the name of the automatically created NAS PV.
> If you need to mount different subdirectories of the same NAS file system to different pods, you must create a separate PVC for each pod. For example, create **pvc-1** for **nginx-1** and **pvc-2** for **nginx-2**.

**Use a filesystem dynamic NAS volume**

> **Important:** When a filesystem-type dynamic NAS volume is deleted, the file system and mount target are retained by default. To release the NAS file system and mount target when the PV is released, you must set `reclaimPolicy` to `Delete` and `deleteVolume` to `true` in the StorageClass.

A pod that uses a filesystem-type NAS volume can create only one file system and one one mount target.
1. **Optional:** Configure and grant a RAM policy.
Filesystem-type NAS volumes involve the dynamic creation and deletion of NAS file systems and mount targets. You must grant the csi-provisioner the necessary permissions. The following is the minimum set of permissions required in the RAM policy. `{`

```json
    "Action": [
        "nas:DescribeMountTargets",
        "nas:CreateMountTarget",
        "nas:DeleteFileSystem",
        "nas:DeleteMountTarget",
        "nas:CreateFileSystem"
```

`],`

```json
    "Resource": [
        "*"
```

`],`

```json
        "Effect": "Allow"
```

`}` You can grant permissions in one of the following ways: Edit the custom policy of the Master RAM role to add the preceding NAS-related permissions. Create a RAM user, grant the RAM policy described above, generate an AccessKey, and configure the AccessKey in the `env` variable of csi-provisioner.

```
env:
- name: CSI_ENDPOINT
  value: unix://socketDir/csi.sock
- name: ACCESS_KEY_ID
  value: ""
- name: ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  value: ""
```

2. Create a StorageClass.
i. Create a file named alicloud-nas-fs.yaml and copy the following content into it.

```
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1 kind: StorageClass metadata:
  name: alicloud-nas-fs
mountOptions:
- nolock,tcp,noresvport
- vers=3
parameters:
  volumeAs: filesystem
  fileSystemType: standard
  storageType: Performance
  regionId: cn-beijing
  zoneId: cn-beijing-e
  vpcId: "vpc-2ze2fxn6popm8c2mzm****"
  vSwitchId: "vsw-2zwdg25a2b4y5juy****"
  accessGroupName: DEFAULT_VPC_GROUP_NAME
  deleteVolume: "false"
provisioner: nasplugin.csi.alibabacloud.com reclaimPolicy: Retain
```

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| volumeAs | Defines the type of volume to create. Valid values: filesystem and subpath . filesystem : The provisioner automatically creates a NAS file system. One PV corresponds to one NAS file system. subpath : The provisioner automatically creates a subdirectory in a NAS file system. One PV corresponds to one subdirectory. |
| fileSystemType | Defines the type of NAS file system to create. Valid values: standard and extreme . standard : General-purpose NAS extreme : Extreme NAS The default value is General-purpose NAS. |
| storageType | Specifies the storage type of the NAS file system. If fileSystemType is standard , valid values are Performance and Capacity . The default value is Performance . If fileSystemType is extreme , valid values are standard and advanced . The default value is standard . |
| regionId | The region where the NAS file system is created. |
| zoneId | The zone where the NAS file system is created. |
| vpcId | The VPC where the mount target of the NAS file system is located. |
| vSwitchId | The ID of the vSwitch where the mount target of the NAS file system is located. |
| accessGroupName | The access group used by the mount target. The default value is DEFAULT VPC GROUP NAME. _ _ _ |

|   | fileSystemType |
|---|---|
| Capacity |   |

|   | fileSystemType |
|---|---|
| advanced |   |

| deleteVolume | Defines the policy for handling the NAS file system when the volume is deleted. This parameter must be configured as a safeguard because NAS is a shared file system. |
|---|---|
| provisioner | Driver type. In this example, the value is nasplugin.csi.alibabacloud.com , which indicates that the Alibaba Cloud NAS CSI plugin is used. |
| reclaimPolicy | The reclaim policy of the PV. The NAS file system is deleted when the PVC is deleted only if this value is Delete and deleteVolume is true . |

ii. Run the following command to create the StorageClass:

```bash
kubectl create -f alicloud-nas-fs.yaml
```

3. Create a PVC and a pod to mount the NAS volume.
i. Create a file named pvc.yaml and copy the following content into it.

```
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim apiVersion: v1 metadata:
  name: nas-csi-pvc-fs
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteMany
  storageClassName: alicloud-nas-fs
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 20Gi
```

ii. Create a file named nginx.yaml and copy the following content into it.

```
apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata:
  name: deployment-nas-fs
  labels:
    app: nginx
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: anolis-registry.cn-zhangjiakou.cr.aliyuncs.com/openanolis/nginx:1.14.1-8.6
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        volumeMounts:
          - name: nas-pvc
            mountPath: "/data"
      volumes:
        - name: nas-pvc
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: nas-csi-pvc-fs
```

iii. Run the following command to create the PVC and pod:

```bash
kubectl create -f pvc.yaml -f nginx.yaml
```

In this scenario, the CSI provisioner dynamically creates a NAS file system and a mount target when the PVC is created, and deletes them when the PVC is deleted.

**Verify NAS data persistence**

NAS provides persistent storage. If a pod is deleted, the newly deployed pod can access the same data because it mounts the same persistent volume. Follow this example to verify the persistence of NAS storage.


3. Run the following command to check the files in the /data directory of the `deployment-nas-1-5b5cdb85f6-`

**Verify NAS shared storage**

A NAS volume can be mounted by multiple pods simultaneously, providing shared storage. When one pod modifies data, the changes are immediately visible to all other pods that mount the same volume. Follow this example to verify the shared storage feature of NAS volumes.
1. View the application pods and NAS files.
i. Run the following command to view the names of the application pods:

```bash
kubectl get pod
```

Expected output:

```
NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE deployment-nas-1-5b5cdb85f6-n**** 1/1 Running 0 32s deployment-nas-2-c5bb4746c-4**** 1/1 Running 0 32s
```

ii. Run the following commands to check the files in the /data directory of both pods:

```bash

```

2. Run the following command to create a file named nas in the /data directory of one of the pods:

```bash
 kubectl exec deployment-nas-1-5b5cdb85f6-n**** -- touch /data/nas
```

3. Run the following commands to check the files in the /data directory of both pods again.
i. Run the following command to check the files in the /data directory of the `deployment-nas-1-` `5b5cdb85f6-n****` pod:

```bash
kubectl exec deployment-nas-1-5b5cdb85f6-n**** -- ls /data
```

Expected output:

```
nas
```

ii. Run the following command to check the files in the /data directory of the `deployment-nas-2-c5bb4746c-` `4****` pod:

```bash
kubectl exec deployment-nas-2-c5bb4746c-4**** -- ls /data
```

Expected output:

```
nas
```

The file created in the /data directory of one pod also exists in the /data directory of the other pod. This confirms that both pods share the same NAS volume.

#### 7.6.5 Mount a statically provisioned OSS volume

Object Storage Service (OSS) volumes can be mounted to multiple pods. OSS is suitable for data that is frequently read but does not require high disk IOPS, such as configuration files, videos, and images. You can use RAM Roles for Service Accounts (RRSA) authentication or AccessKey pair authentication to mount statically provisioned OSS volumes to your applications.

**Prerequisites**

The Kubernetes version of the cluster is 1.26 or later. The version of the Container Storage Interface (CSI) plug-in is v1.31.4-9819c8b-aliyun or later.

> **Note:** ACK clusters that run Kubernetes 1.26 or higher allow you to mount volumes by using RRSA authentication. ACK clusters that run other Kubernetes versions allow you to mount volumes by using AccessKey pair authentication.

An OSS bucket is created. The OSS bucket and ACK cluster belong to the same Apsara Stack tenant account. For more information, see **Create a bucket** in the Buckets chapter of OSS User Guide.

**Mount a volume using RRSA authentication**

The RAM Roles for Service Accounts (RRSA) feature lets you implement OpenAPI permission isolation at the persistent volume (PV) level within a cluster. This feature provides fine-grained isolation for cloud resource access permissions and helps reduce security risks.
1. Enable the RRSA feature. For more information, see the Enable RRSA section in the Use RRSA to authorize
different pods to access different cloud services topic.
2. Create a RAM role for mounting OSS volumes using RRSA authentication. The RAM role is assumed by
your cluster when it uses RRSA to mount OSS volumes. For more information, see Step 2: Create a RAM role and grant the required permissions.
3. Use RRSA to mount an OSS bucket as a statically provisioned volume. For more information, see Step 3:
Use RRSA to mount an OSS bucket as a statically provisioned volume.

**Use AccessKey pair authentication to mount a statically provisioned OSS**

**volume**

> **Important:** If the AccessKey pair referenced by the OSS volume is revoked or the required permissions are revoked, the application to which the volume is mounted fails to access OSS, and a permission error is reported. To resolve the issue, you need to modify the Secret that stores the AccessKey pair and mount the OSS volume to the application again. In this case, the application is restarted.
> To regularly rotate AccessKey pairs**,** we recommend that you use RRSA authentication.

**Step 1: Confirm the required permissions**

1. Obtain the AccessKey pair that is required to access OSS buckets. To obtain your AccessKey pair, log in to
the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, choose **Enterprise > Resources > Organizations**. In the Organization Structure pane, click the organization and click **Manage Access Key Pairs** in the **Basic**
**Information** section.
2. Grant the AccessKey pair permissions on OSS buckets.
Policy that provides read and write permissions on OSS `{`

```json
    "Statement": [
```

`{`

```json
            "Action": "oss:*",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Resource": [
                "acs:oss:*:*:mybucket",
                "acs:oss:*:*:mybucket/*"
```

`]` `}` `],`

```json
    "Version": "1"
```

`}` Policy that provides read-only permissions on OSS `{`

```json
    "Statement": [
```

`{`

```json
            "Action": [
                "oss:Get*",
                "oss:List*"
```

`],`

```json
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Resource": [
                "acs:oss:*:*:mybucket",
                "acs:oss:*:*:mybucket/*"
```

`]` `}` `],`

```json
    "Version": "1"
```

`}` Optional. If the objects in the OSS bucket are encrypted by using a specified customer master key (CMK) in Key Management Service (KMS), you need to grant KMS access permissions to the RAM user.

**kubectl operations**

1. Create a PV.
i. Create a Secret, which must be created in the namespace in which the application that uses the PV is deployed. Replace the values of the `akId` and `akSecret` parameters with the AccessKey ID and AccessKey secret obtained in the previous step.

```bash
kubectl create secret generic oss-secret --from-literal='akId=<yourAccessKey ID>' --fromliteral='akSecret=<yourAccessKey Secret>'
```

ii. Create a statically provisioned PV.

```bash
kubectl create -f pv-oss.yaml
```

Save the following sample code as a pv-oss.yaml file to create a PV.

```
apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolume metadata:
  name: pv-oss
  labels:
    alicloud-pvname: pv-oss
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 5Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadOnlyMany
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  csi:
    driver: ossplugin.csi.alibabacloud.com
    volumeHandle: pv-oss # The specified value must be the same as the name of the PV.
    nodePublishSecretRef:
      name: oss-secret
      namespace: default
    volumeAttributes:
      bucket: "oss" # Replace the value with the name of the OSS bucket you want to mount.
      url: "oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com"
      otherOpts: "-o umask=022 -o max_stat_cache_size=0 -o allow_other"
      path: "/"
```

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| name | The name of the PV. |
| labels | The labels that are added to the PV. |
| storage | The available storage capacity of the OSS bucket. |
| accessModes | The access mode. Valid values: ReadOnlyMany and ReadWriteMany. If you select ReadOnlyMany, ossfs mounts the OSS bucket in read-only mode. |
| persistentVolumeReclaimPo licy | The reclaim policy of the PV. OSS volumes support only the Retain policy, which indicates that the PV and data in the bucket are not deleted when you delete the PVC. |
| driver | The type of volume driver. In this example, the value is set to ossplugin.csi.alibabacloud.com. This indicates that the OSS CSI plug-in provided by Alibaba Cloud is used. |
| nodePublishSecretRef | The Secret from which the AccessKey pair that the system uses to mount PV is retrieved. |
| volumeHandle | The name of the PV. |
| bucket | The OSS bucket that you want to mount. |

|   | url | The endpoint of the OSS bucket you want to mount. You can retrieve the endpoint from the Overview page of the bucket in the OSS console. The following are the common formats for different access ports: Format of public endpoints: http://oss-{{regionName}}.aliyuncs.com or https://oss-{{regionName}}.aliyuncs.com . |   |   |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|   |   | You can configure custom parameters in the -o *** -o *** format for the OSS volume. Example: -o umask=022 -o max stat cache size=0 -o _ _ _ allow other . _ umask: modifies the permission mask of files in ossfs. For example, if you specify umask=022, the permission mask of files in ossfs changes to 755. By default, the permission mask of files uploaded using the OSS SDK or console is 640 in OSSFS. Therefore, we recommend that you specify the umask parameter if you want to split reads and writes. max stat cache size: the maximum number of files whose metadata can be _ _ _ cached in the metadata cache. Metadata caching can accelerate List operations. However, if you modify files using methods other than ossfs, such as the OSS console, OSS SDK, or ossutil, the metadata of the files may not be updated in real time. allow other: allows other users to access the mounted directory. However, _ these users cannot access the files in the directory. |   |   |
|   |   |   | -o umask=022 -o max stat cache size=0 -o _ _ _ |   |
|   |   | allow other _ |   |   |
|   | otherOpts |   |   |   |
|   | path | The path relative to the root directory of the OSS bucket to be mounted. The default value is /. This parameter is supported by CSI 1.14.8.32-c77e277b-aliyun and later. |   |   |
|   | sigVersion | The request signature version supported by the OSS server. Valid values: "v1": version 1, which is the default value. "v4": Uses OSS Signature Version 4. |   |   |

iii. Create a PVC.

```bash
kubectl create -f pvc-oss.yaml
```

Save the following sample code as a pv-oss.yaml file to create a PVC.

```
apiVersion: v1 kind: PersistentVolume metadata:
  name: pv-oss
  labels:
    alicloud-pvname: pv-oss
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 5Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadOnlyMany
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  csi:
    driver: ossplugin.csi.alibabacloud.com
    volumeHandle: pv-oss # The specified value must be the same as the name of the PV.
    nodePublishSecretRef:
      name: oss-secret
      namespace: default
    volumeAttributes:
      bucket: "oss" # Replace the value with the name of the OSS bucket you want to mount.
      url: "oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com"
      otherOpts: "-o umask=022 -o max_stat_cache_size=0 -o allow_other"
      path: "/"
```

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| name | The name of the PVC. |
| accessModes | The access mode. Valid values: ReadOnlyMany and ReadWriteMany. If you select ReadOnlyMany, ossfs mounts the OSS bucket in read-only mode. |
| storage | The declared application usage cannot exceed the total capacity of the persistent volume. |
| alicloud-pvname | The labels that are used to select and bind a PV to the PVC. The labels must be the same as those of the PV to be bound to the PVC. |

iv. Create an application named oss-static and mount the PV to the application.

```bash
kubectl create -f oss-static.yaml
```

Sample configurations in the oss-static.yaml file:

```
apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata:
  name: oss-static
  labels:
    app: nginx
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: anolis-registry.cn-zhangjiakou.cr.aliyuncs.com/openanolis/nginx:1.14.1-8.6
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        volumeMounts:
          - name: pvc-oss
            mountPath: "/data"
          - name: pvc-oss
            mountPath: "/data1"
        livenessProbe:
          exec:
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - cd /data
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 30
      volumes:
        - name: pvc-oss
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: pvc-oss
```

`livenessProbe` : Configure health checks. `mountPath` : the path where the OSS bucket is mounted in the container. `claimName` : the name of the PVC that the application uses.

#### 7.6.6 Mount a dynamically provisioned OSS volume

Object Storage Service (OSS) volumes can be mounted to multiple pods. OSS is suitable for data that is frequently read but does not require high disk IOPS, such as configuration files, videos, and images. In addition to static provisioning, you can use dynamic provisioning to configure the system to automatically reserve persistent volumes (PVs) based on persistent volume claims (PVCs) and StorageClasses. You can use RAM Roles for Service Accounts (RRSA) authentication or AccessKey pair authentication to mount dynamically provisioned OSS volumes to your applications.

**Prerequisites**

The Kubernetes version of the cluster is 1.26 or later. The version of the Container Storage Interface (CSI) plug-in is v1.31.4-9819c8b-aliyun or later.

> **Note:** ACK clusters that run Kubernetes 1.26 or higher allow you to mount volumes by using RRSA authentication. ACK clusters that run other Kubernetes versions allow you to mount volumes by using AccessKey pair authentication.

An OSS bucket is created. The OSS bucket and ACK cluster belong to the same Apsara Stack tenant account. For more information, see **Create a bucket** in the Buckets chapter of OSS User Guide.

**Use AccessKey pair authentication to mount a dynamically provisioned**

**OSS volume**

> **Important:** If the AccessKey pair referenced by the OSS volume is revoked or the required permissions are revoked, the application to which the volume is mounted fails to access OSS, and a permission error is reported. To resolve the issue, you need to modify the Secret that stores the AccessKey pair and mount the OSS volume to the application again. In this case, the application is restarted.
> If you need to regularly rotate AccessKey pairs**,** we recommend that you use RRSA authentication.

**Step 1: Confirm the required permissions**

1. Obtain the AccessKey pair that is required to access OSS buckets. To obtain your AccessKey pair, log in to
the Apsara Uni-manager Management Console, choose **Enterprise > Resources > Organizations**. In the Organization Structure pane, click the organization and click **Manage Access Key Pairs** in the **Basic**
**Information** section.
2. Grant the AccessKey pair permissions on OSS buckets.
Policy that provides read and write permissions on OSS `{`

```json
    "Statement": [
```

`{`

```json
            "Action": "oss:*",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Resource": [
                "acs:oss:*:*:mybucket",
                "acs:oss:*:*:mybucket/*"
```

`]` `}` `],`

```json
    "Version": "1"
```

`}` Policy that provides read-only permissions on OSS `{`

```json
    "Statement": [
```

`{`

```json

                "oss:Get*",
                "oss:List*"
```

`],`

```json
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Resource": [
                "acs:oss:*:*:mybucket",
                "acs:oss:*:*:mybucket/*"
```

`]` `}` `],`

```json
    "Version": "1"
```

`}` Optional. If the objects in the OSS bucket are encrypted by using a specified customer master key (CMK) in Key Management Service (KMS), you need to grant KMS access permissions to the RAM user.

**Step 2: Create a StorageClass and a PVC, and use the StorageClass and**

**the PVC to mount the OSS bucket to an application**

**Console operations**

1. Create a StorageClass.
i. Log in to the ACK console. In the left-side navigation pane, click **Clusters**. ii. On the **Clusters** page, click the ACK dedicated cluster that you want to manage. In the left-side navigation pane of the cluster details page, choose **Volumes > StorageClasses**. iii. In the upper-right corner of the **StorageClasses** page, click **Create**. iv. In the dialog box that appears, configure the parameters and click **Create**.

Valid values: Select Existing Secret: If you select this option, you must also configure the Namespace and Secret parameters. Create Secret: If you select this option, you must also configure the Namespace, Name, AccessKey ID, and AccessKey Secret parameters. | Select Existing Secret |

All volumes share the same path. This means that data is stored at <bucket>:<path>/ . Subdirectory: The OSS volume is mounted in subpath mode.
